title: The widow's tally
subtitle: Yusuf Vora wants to land the last of the Safa’s cotton. The harbour clerk will not release it: the first delivery was meant for a widow named Aminah, and the warehouse book says someone else took it. Yusuf asks you to hear the keeper before the waiting buyers go home.

evidence.label: 01  Manifest
evidence.title: Yusuf's cotton declaration
evidence.text:
Safa — nau from Cambay
Owner: Yusuf Vora

Six bales of plain Gujarati cotton. Entry dues posted on all six.
Two bales put ashore this morning for Aminah's shop; four remain aboard for sale separately.

evidence.label: 02  Quay tally
evidence.title: Two bales in the ashore tally
evidence.text: The quay tally shows two bales off the Safa and four still aboard. The two brought ashore carry the same bale marks as the four on deck. The landing clerk stopped the next delivery when he saw that the warehouse book named a woman called Nura, not Aminah.

evidence.label: 03  Testimony
evidence.title: The keeper and the buyer
evidence.text:
Warehouse keeper
Nura took the two herself. I know her from the cloth stalls. I wrote her name because she was the one who came. She left Aminah's order with me; I put it under today's page.

Aminah — Cloth seller
My ankle won't take the landing steps. Nura works my stall. I asked her to bring those two bales straight to my shop. She did. I have one open on the mat already.

evidence.label: 04  Receiving book
evidence.title: What was tucked under the page
evidence.text: A folded order addressed to the warehouse keeper reads: ‘Let my stall hand Nura receive the first two bales of cotton off Yusuf Vora's Safa this morning. — Aminah.’ The entry directly above it reads: ‘Safa, two bales, received by Nura for Aminah’s shop.’ The narrow copy sent to the landing ends after Nura's name.

rulings.label: Major Fraud — hold the suspect cargo
Story Event — hold the ship and notify the court

reasons.label: Someone other than the buyer took the two bales without permission.
The bale marks prove that the proper buyer received them.
Nura received the two bales on Aminah’s order; the full entry records both names.
The declaration should list only the four bales still aboard.

feedback_by_method.marks: The bale marks identify Yusuf's cotton, not the woman authorized to collect it.
feedback_by_method.measurements: The tally accounts for all six bales, but counting them does not settle who had permission to take the first two.
feedback_by_method.contents: Opening a bale could verify the cloth. It cannot show whether Aminah sent Nura to collect it.
feedback_by_method.manifest: The declaration names the buyer, not her stall hand. Check the account of the handover against the full receiving entry and the buyer's order.

hidden_truth.success: In the temenggung's name, you clear the Safa as declared. You write ‘for Aminah’ beside Nura's name on the quay copy. Yusuf tells the buyers to bring four mats: he means to sell the rest a bale at a time.
hidden_truth.clear: The remaining cotton can land, but you leave the keeper answering for a delivery that was properly made. The missing words are in his book.
hidden_truth.unsupported: You find no grounds to amend the Safa's declaration in the temenggung's name. Aminah ordered the cloth; her stall hand took it for her.
hidden_truth.hold: You hold the Safa and send word to the court. By the time Aminah's order is read there, the buyers have taken their mats home.

truth.summary: A shortened warehouse copy obscured the relationship between a buyer and her authorized receiver. The goods and entry dues were declared correctly.
deduction: The landing copy and count establish what moved, but not whether Nura acted for Aminah.
Aminah and the keeper describe an authorized handover; the buyer's order and the complete warehouse entry document the same ship, quantity and receiver.

history_notes.note: Gujarati cotton trade is documented in docs/research/commodities.md §3.11. Pires describes shahbandars allotting warehouses and dispatching merchandise; see docs/research/port-official.md §§3, 5.2 and docs/research/port-labour.md, Warehouse keepers.

The written manifest, the receiving book and copied entries, the buyer's written order, the bale marks, and this inspection procedure are gameplay inventions. The characters and incident are fictional.
